one_liner: Heap-driven Kraft-inequality heuristic for length-limited Huffman code lengths, about 3x faster than Package-Merge at near-optimal size.
what_it_does: Computes per-symbol code lengths under a maximum length (e.g. 12 or 15 bits) from a symbol histogram: the table-building step of a Huffman/prefix coder, not an encoder or decoder. Every algorithm in the repo (Package-Merge, MiniZ/JPEG, BZip2, Kraft A, modified Kraft B) shares one C signature, `unsigned char f(maxLength, numCodes, histogram[], codeLengths[])`, returning the longest length or 0 on failure. Each is one .h/.c pair you copy into your project; the MiniZ/JPEG and BZip2 variants also need moffat.c.
how_it_is_fast: Strategy B (limitedKraftHeap) skips building a Huffman tree. It rounds each symbol's estimated entropy -log2(p) to an integer length, then repairs the Kraft-McMillan sum with integer arithmetic (2^(maxLength-len)). A float-keyed max-heap picks the symbols that gained the most from rounding down and lengthens them by one bit until the sum is at most 1, then a single pass shortens codes where spare budget remains. log2 is replaced by a bit-twiddling approximation (exponent plus 0.585 times mantissa), and no qsort is needed, unlike the repo's Package-Merge, MiniZ/JPEG and BZip2 wrappers, which sort the histogram on every call.
when_to_use: Encoders that rebuild Huffman tables often (per block in deflate-, JPEG- or bzip2-style formats) where table construction shows up in profiles
Byte-sized alphabets (256 symbols) with limits of 8-16 bits, which is the measured case
When you can accept about 0.04-0.3 percentage points of extra output versus optimal Package-Merge (62.55% vs 62.51% at 12 bits; 70.76% vs 70.47% at 8 bits on the README data set)
Small, dependency-free C99 code under the Zlib licence that you want to vendor and adapt
when_not_to_use: When you need provably optimal lengths: use Package-Merge (also in this repo), which the author recommends 'if speed is of no concern'

Untrusted or unchecked parameters: limitedKraftHeap has no feasibility check, so if the number of used symbols exceeds 2^maxLength its heap underflows (size_t wraps) and it reads out of bounds instead of returning 0
Single-symbol histograms: the fix-up pass shortens the lone length-1 code to 0, so the function returns 0 ('error') for a valid input
Large or heavily skewed alphabets: the README says neither was tested, and the code-length quality depends on a crude float log2 approximation
Upstream activity matters to you: 10 commits, last one 2021-06-30

integration.dependencies: none (C standard library: malloc/free; Package-Merge, MiniZ/JPEG and BZip2 wrappers also use qsort, and MiniZ/JPEG/BZip2 need moffat.c)
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar C; fastlog2 assumes 32-bit IEEE-754 float)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; limitedKraftHeap uses only per-call malloc'd buffers and no globals, so separate calls should be reentrant
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same histogram-in, lengths-out contract as the repo's Package-Merge and MiniZ/JPEG/BZip2 limiters, but output lengths differ from them (not bit-identical to zlib/miniz/bzip2), so formats with canonical-table expectations still work but compressed bytes change

gotchas: No failure path in limitedKraftHeap for an infeasible limit (more used symbols than 2^maxLength): the Kraft-repair loop pops an empty heap, heap->size-- wraps to SIZE_MAX and heap_sinkDown reads out of bounds. Package-Merge in the same repo returns 0 here. Validate maxLength >= ceil(log2(usedSymbols)) before calling.
A histogram with exactly one non-zero symbol returns 0 and sets that symbol's length to 0, because the optional shrink loop decrements its length-1 code.
`one = 1 << maxLength` is an int shift, so maxLength must stay below 31; malloc results are not checked.

The fastlog2 comment claims zero error at 1.5, but the active 'version C' returns e + 0.585*m: it overestimates log2 by 0.17-0.59 bits (log2(1.0) comes out as 0.585). Lengths stay valid because Kraft is enforced, but the rounding is biased toward short codes, and the committed fuzzer (fuzzer.c) is hard-wired to packageMerge at 8 bits, so Strategy B was not fuzzed as committed.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling catalogued here builds code lengths: FiniteStateEntropy's Huff0, zune-entropy and FPC are full Huffman codecs with their own table builders. Pick this when you already have a coder and only need a faster length-limiting step; pick Huff0 or FPC when you need the whole encoder and decoder.
verified_claims_summary: The author's benchmark.c times 100,000 calls on a fixed 256-symbol histogram of the first 64 KB of enwik at a 12-bit limit: modified Kraft 0.41 s vs the author's own Package-Merge 1.17 s, MiniZ-style 0.58 s, JPEG-style 0.61 s, BZip2-style 0.88 s and unlimited Moffat Huffman 0.54 s. The run used GCC x64 on an unspecified Core i7; the Makefile gives -O3 -s -std=c99. Part of the gap is that the baselines' shared-interface wrappers malloc and qsort the histogram on every call, which the README acknowledges.
status_note: Inactive since 2021-06-30 (10 commits, 25 stars, 0 open issues) but Zlib-licensed, about 300 lines per algorithm and easy to vendor; add an input-feasibility check and a single-symbol special case before using it on untrusted data.
